title: Schellang and Sharkey; drumming then and now
summary: Sal recounts Schellang's disappearance and return, and says drumming has changed, naming Joe Morello as best.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I heard some different stories about him.

He was lost for a long time. Nobody knew where he was. Then he came back to town. I tell you, Shalang, I mean, what's the name of my Sharky? You tell yourself. Sharky only used three drummers, man, all the time. He was the Levite amongst his, all the Shalang. Sharky and Shalang were like that. I was surprised, when all he come back, that he didn't play with Sharky anymore. At all. Now, he couldn't play anymore, either. I tell you, I tell you. But one time he played fine drums, man. He played with Sharky at the race. He played with Winging in Chicago.
He played with Winging in Chicago, that one.

He played fine drums. I thought. He wasn't a technician, you know. In those days, you see, drumming is changed a lot. In those days, good drummers would have good solid beats, steady. Today, good drummers, the guys can play a lot of stuff. Well, I never could do that. Never. I only knew one guy that wants to do that. There were two guys, Levi and Ray. Today, they're down the top. Now, this reel's almost double with. Today, the guys fast. I think I heard the best. Joe Morello, Shadow Man.
